root_cause_criterion.criterion: Once `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` transfers DH ownership into `peer_tmp`, the local alias `dh` must be cleared before any post-assignment error path can reach the shared `err:` cleanup.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original leaves `dh` non-NULL after `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)`, so the later weak-key error path still frees the transferred object once through `DH_free(dh)` and again through `EVP_PKEY_free(peer_tmp)`. The fixed original sets `dh = NULL`, leaving the transferred DH object owned only by `peer_tmp` on the shared cleanup path.

nodes.state: The shared `err:` cleanup reaches `DH_free(dh)` while the local alias still names the transferred `DH` object, so this first cleanup call releases that object before owner cleanup runs.
Owner cleanup next calls `DH_free(pkey->pkey.dh)` on the same `DH *` pointer that the local cleanup already freed, re-entering `DH_free` with a stale object pointer.

The second `DH_free` reaches `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF(&r->references, &i, r->lock)` while `r` still names the freed `DH` object, so the immediately following inline refcount decrement produces the AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free WRITE.

edges.relation: The post-assignment local `dh` alias persists unchanged to `DH_free(dh)` in the shared cleanup, so the first cleanup call acts on the transferred object instead of NULL.
After the shared cleanup frees the transferred `DH` through `dh`, owner cleanup later reaches `DH_free(pkey->pkey.dh)` with that same stale pointer.
The owner-cleanup `DH_free(pkey->pkey.dh)` call forwards that same `DH` object's `references` slot into `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF(&r->references, &i, r->lock)`, where the stale refcount write occurs.
